questions.question:
Select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of idioms/phrases.

At sixes and sevens

options.text: If someone is anxious before sitting an examination
If someone is in a state of confusion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **If someone is in a state of confusion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"At sixes and sevens"** means to be in a state of confusion or disorder. (अव्यवस्था या भ्रम की स्थिति)
 
 
• **Example:** After the sudden change in the project plan, the team was at sixes and sevens about how to proceed.
 
 
• The correct meaning aligns with the context of confusion or disorganization. (भ्रम या अव्यवस्था का संदर्भ)
 
 
• **Example:** The office was at sixes and sevens after the manager announced his resignation.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **If someone is in a state of confusion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** If someone is anxious before sitting an examination (कोई परीक्षा देने से पहले चिंतित)
 
 
• **Example:** He was anxious before his final exam but managed to calm down afterward.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** If someone is in depression (कोई अवसाद में है)
 
 
• **Example:** She has been in depression since the loss of her pet.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** If someone is super happy (कोई बहुत खुश है)
 
 
• **Example:** He was super happy after receiving the promotion at work.

questions.question:
Choose the option that has an error in the sentence.

On the plus side, if this development are getting better, the richer nations will benefit.

options.text: if this development are getting better,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the **subject-verb agreement** within the conditional clause of the sentence.
 
• The noun "**development**" is a singular countable noun in this context, which requires the singular auxiliary verb "**is**."
 
• The use of the plural verb "**are**" is grammatically incorrect when paired with a singular subject.
 
• Therefore, "**are getting better**" should be corrected to "**is getting better**" to maintain grammatical consistency.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"On the plus side, if this development **is getting** better, the richer nations will benefit."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "On the plus side,"** – This is a correct idiomatic expression used to introduce a positive aspect of a situation.
 
• **Option 3: "the richer nations will benefit."** – This part is grammatically correct. It follows the structure of a **First Conditional** sentence (If + present tense, will + base verb), which describes a possible future outcome.
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:** Always identify the head noun of the subject phrase. Since "development" is singular, the verb must also be singular, regardless of any surrounding descriptive words.

questions.question:
Examine the given sentence and pick out the error.

In order to overcome the mental depression and stress (1) adapting meditation, yoga or (2) similar other methods (3) can be helped

options.text: in order to overcome the mental depression and stress

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase "**can be helped**," which uses the **passive voice** incorrectly.
 
• In this sentence, the practices (meditation, yoga, etc.) are the subjects that perform the action of helping. Therefore, the verb should be in the **active voice** ("**can help**").
 
• "Can be helped" implies that someone or something is providing assistance *to* the methods, which makes the sentence logically nonsensical.
 
• Additionally, there is a lexical error in **Option 1**: "**adapting**" should be "**adopting**." To "adopt" a practice means to start using it, while to "adapt" means to modify something. However, the structural error in the verb phrase (Option 2) is typically considered the primary grammatical flaw in such tests.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"In order to overcome mental depression and stress, **adopting** meditation, yoga or similar other methods **can help**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "adapting meditation, yoga or"** – As noted, "adopting" is the more precise word here, but often in objective tests, the voice error in the predicate is the targeted answer.
 
• **Option 3: "in order to overcome the mental depression and stress"** – This part is grammatically acceptable. While the definite article "the" is optional before "mental depression," its presence is not a technical error.
 
• **Option 4: "similar other methods"** – This phrase correctly serves as a collective category for other activities like meditation and yoga.
 
• **Grammar Note:** Always ensure the **subject** (the methods) and the **verb** (help) have a logical relationship. If the subject is the "doer," use active voice.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The proposal was rejected ________ grounds of insufficient evidence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**on**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The preposition "**on**" is used when referring to the basis or grounds for something, such as a decision or conclusion.
 
• In the context of the sentence, "**on grounds of insufficient evidence**" is the correct phrase to indicate the reason for the rejection.
 
• **Options 1, 3,** and **4** are incorrect as they do not fit the established usage of prepositions in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The proposal was rejected **on**__ grounds of insufficient evidence."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "by"** is incorrect because "by" is used to indicate the agent performing an action, not the grounds or basis.
 
• **Option 3: "in"** is incorrect as it does not fit the phrase "grounds of insufficient evidence."
 
• **Option 4: "under"** is incorrect because "under" is used to describe rules, conditions, or authority, not the basis of rejection.
</ul

questions.question: Choose the odd one out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary distinction between the given words is their **phonetic pronunciation**.
 
• The words **Knight**, **Night**, and **Nite** are all **homophones**, meaning they are pronounced identically as **/naɪt/** despite their different spellings and meanings.
 
• The word **Knit** is pronounced as **/nɪt/**, utilizing a short "i" vowel sound, which makes it phonetically different from the others.
 
• Since it does not share the same pronunciation as the rest of the group, **Knit** is the odd one out.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Knight:** A historical term for a man-at-arms or a modern title of honor; it contains a silent 'k' and 'gh'.
 
• **Night:** The period from sunset to sunrise; it also contains a silent 'gh'.
 
• **Nite:** An informal or simplified spelling of "night," often used in advertising or branding.
 
• **Knit:** To interlock loops of yarn with needles; while it shares a silent 'k' with "Knight," its vowel sound remains distinct.

questions.question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The two sisters decided to divide the stolen money among themselves.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**between themselves**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The phrase "**between themselves**" is used when referring to an action or division occurring among two individuals or parties.
 
• The word "**among**" is typically used for more than two entities, whereas "**between**" is appropriate for two.
 
• In the context of the sentence, the division of money is happening between the two sisters, making "**between themselves**" the correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The two sisters decided to divide the stolen money **between themselves**__."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "into themselves"** is incorrect as "into" implies movement inside, which is not applicable in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "for themselves"** is incorrect as it changes the meaning, implying the money was taken for their use, rather than divided.
 
• **Option 4: "No substitution"** is incorrect because the phrase "among themselves" is grammatically inappropriate for two individuals.
</ul

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

The strong current of the river broke through the wall of the earthen dam within no time.

options.text: The wall of the earthen dam was broken within no time by the strong current of the river.
The wall of the earthen dam was broken through within no time by the strong current of the river.
The wall of the earthen dam had broken through within no time by the strong current of the river.
The wall of the earthen dam had been broken through within no time by the strong current of the river.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The strong current of the river broke through the wall of the earthen dam within no time."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the wall of the earthen dam" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "broke through" to "was broken through" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the strong current of the river."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "within no time" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The wall of the earthen dam was broken through within no time by the strong current of the river."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The wall of the earthen dam was broken within no time by the strong current of the river." – Missing "through," incorrect phrasing.
 
• **Option 3: **"The wall of the earthen dam had broken through within no time by the strong current of the river." – Incorrect tense (past perfect active).
 
• **Option 4: **"The wall of the earthen dam had been broken through within no time by the strong current of the river." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).

3d:T

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

The mystery had never been solved by anyone before the detective arrived.

options.text: No one never solved the mystery before the detective arrived.
No one had solved the mystery before the detective arrived.
No one solves the mystery before the detective arrived.
No one has solved the mystery before the detective arrived.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence provided is in passive voice: "The mystery had never been solved by anyone before the detective arrived."
 
• To convert it into active voice, the subject of the passive sentence ("anyone") becomes the active subject.
 
• The verb form "had never been solved" must be changed to "had solved" in the past perfect tense.
 
• The sentence "No one had solved the mystery before the detective arrived" correctly preserves the original meaning while converting to active voice.
 
• Option 2 is grammatically correct and aligns with the tense and context of the original sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"No one had solved the mystery before the detective arrived."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "No one never solved the mystery before the detective arrived." – Incorrect due to the use of double negatives ("no one" and "never").
 
• **Option 3:** "No one solves the mystery before the detective arrived." – Incorrect tense ("solves" is present tense, which conflicts with "arrived").
 
• **Option 4:** "No one has solved the mystery before the detective arrived." – Incorrect tense ("has solved" is present perfect, which does not match the past tense of "arrived").

3e:T

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Sairam said, "She has to come to Delhi to me within the next couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she mentioned."

options.text: Sairam said that she had to come to Delhi to her within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.
Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to bring help to solve the problem she had mentioned
Sairam said that she has to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she mentioned.
Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The process of converting direct speech into indirect speech involves changing pronouns, time expressions, and verb tenses accordingly.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"She has to come" becomes "she had to go":**
 
 
• The verb "has to" (present obligation) changes to "had to" (past obligation).
 
• "come" changes to "go" since the reporting speaker (Sairam) is referring to a location different from his own.
 
 
 
• **"to me" becomes "to him":**
 
 
• The pronoun "me" changes to "him" as Sairam is being referred to in the third person.
 
 
 
• **"within the next couple of hours" becomes "within the following couple of hours":**
 
 
• Time expressions like "next" change to "following" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged, as it appropriately conveys the statement in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Indirect speech does not use quotation marks.
 
• The sentence structure is adjusted to align with the grammatical rules of indirect narration.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Sairam said that she had to come to Delhi to her within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned." 
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun usage: "to her" instead of "to him" disrupts the meaning.
 
• "come" should be changed to "go" in indirect narration, as the perspective shifts.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to bring help to solve the problem she had mentioned." 
 
 
• Incorrect verb usage: "bring help" instead of "take help" alters the context.
 
• Time expression "next" should be "following" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Sairam said that she has to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she mentioned." 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "has to" should be "had to" in indirect speech.
 
• Time expression "next" should be "following" in indirect speech.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He exclaimed with regret that he had forgotten his wallet at home.

options.text: He exclaimed, "Hey! I had forgotten my wallet at home.
He said, "Oh no! I have forgotten my wallet at home."
He exclaimed, "Ah! I have forgot my wallet at home."
He said, "I regret I have forgotten my wallet at home."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The sentence in direct speech must accurately reflect the tone and meaning of the original indirect speech.
 
• **Key Conversion:**
 
 
• **Reporting verb:** In the indirect speech, "exclaimed with regret" conveys emotion. In direct speech, this is replaced with "Oh no!" to express the same regret in a conversational manner.
 
• **Tense:** The indirect speech uses "had forgotten," which in direct speech is converted to "have forgotten" to match the conversational present perfect tense.
 
• **Pronouns:** The pronoun "he" in indirect speech is replaced with "I" in direct speech to reflect the speaker's perspective.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with an exclamation "Oh no!" to express regret.
 
• Proper sentence structure and tense are maintained.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**He said, "Oh no! I have forgotten my wallet at home.*"

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Hey! I had forgotten my wallet at home." 

 
 
• Incorrect tone. "Hey!" does not convey regret, and "had forgotten" is not appropriate for direct conversational speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Ah! I have forgot my wallet at home." 
 
 
• Incorrect verb form. "forgot" should be "forgotten" in present perfect tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "I regret I have forgotten my wallet at home." 
 
 
• Lacks conversational tone and does not fully convey the emotion expressed in the original sentence.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

She told the detective that she had been sleeping when the thieves had broken in.

options.text: She said to the detective, "I had slept when the thieves had broken in."
She said to the detective, "I had slept when the thieves has broken in."
She told the detective, "I had been sleeping when the thieves broke in."
She told the detective, "I had been asleep when the thieves were breaking in."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Understanding Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• Indirect speech converts the original sentence into reported speech, focusing on the meaning rather than the exact words.
 
• The tense of verbs in indirect speech is typically adjusted to reflect the time the original statement was made.
 
 
 
• **Direct Speech Conversion:**
 
 
• To convert to direct speech, the sentence must reflect the exact words spoken by the subject.
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker mentioned: "I had been sleeping when the thieves broke in."
 
 
 
• **Correct Choice:** Option 3 accurately converts the indirect speech into direct speech while maintaining tense and context.
 
 
• "I had been sleeping" retains the past perfect continuous tense, reflecting an ongoing action in the past.
 
• "The thieves broke in" correctly uses the simple past tense for the action that occurred simultaneously.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She told the detective, 'I had been sleeping when the thieves broke in.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said to the detective, 'I had slept when the thieves had broken in.'"
 
 
• Incorrect tense usage: "had slept" suggests a completed action before the thieves broke in, which changes the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She said to the detective, 'I had slept when the thieves has broken in.'"
 
 
• Grammatical error: "has broken in" incorrectly uses present perfect tense instead of past tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She told the detective, 'I had been asleep when the thieves were breaking in.'"
 
 
• Incorrect phrasing: "were breaking in" uses past continuous tense, which suggests the action was ongoing, altering the original meaning.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The groundbreaking quantum theory should not have been dismissed as mere speculation by the scientific community.

options.text: The scientific community should not have been dismissing the groundbreaking quantum theory as mere speculation.
The scientific community should not have dismissed the groundbreaking quantum theory as mere speculation.
The groundbreaking quantum theory should not be dismissed as mere speculation by the scientific community.
The scientific community should not be dismissing the groundbreaking quantum theory as mere speculation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• Active voice structure: The subject of the sentence performs the action, while the object receives it. 
 
• The passive voice sentence is: "The groundbreaking quantum theory should not have been dismissed as mere speculation by the scientific community." 
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the original subject "the scientific community" at the beginning of the sentence. 
 
• Change the passive verb form "should not have been dismissed" to "should not have dismissed" (active voice form). 
 
• Ensure the object "the groundbreaking quantum theory" remains after the verb for clarity. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The scientific community should not have dismissed the groundbreaking quantum theory as mere speculation."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: **"The scientific community should not have been dismissing the groundbreaking quantum theory as mere speculation." – Incorrect because it uses the continuous tense unnecessarily. 
 
• **Option 3: **"The groundbreaking quantum theory should not be dismissed as mere speculation by the scientific community." – Incorrect because this is in the present passive voice, not matching the original sentence's tense.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

They had not finished the project before the deadline.

options.text: The project was not finished by them before the deadline.
The project has not been finished by them before the deadline.
The project had not been finished by them before the deadline.
The project was not being finished by them before the deadline.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They had not finished the project before the deadline."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the project" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "had not finished" to "had not been finished" (past perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "them."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "before the deadline" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The project had not been finished by them before the deadline."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The project was not finished by them before the deadline." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"The project has not been finished by them before the deadline." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"The project was not being finished by them before the deadline." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
</ul

questions.question:
In the sentence:

"Engineering was once considered one of the most prestigious and secure career choices in India," what is the tense of the verb "was considered"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2 (Past simple)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Present simple***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Present simple would be “is considered,” but the sentence uses “was considered,” which refers to the past.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Past simple***
 
 
• This is **correct**. “Was considered” is the past simple tense, indicating that engineering was regarded as prestigious in the past, but the perception has changed now.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Past perfect***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Past perfect would be “had been considered,” which is not used here.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Present perfect***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Present perfect would be “has been considered,” but the passage clearly uses “was considered.”
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 (Past simple)**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Past simple tense** is used to describe actions or states that happened at a specific time in the past.
 
• Example: “She was considered the best student in her class.”
 
• In the passage: “Engineering was once considered…” → This shows a past perception that has now changed.

questions.question:
In the sentence:

"Moreover, industries now prefer candidates with practical knowledge and specialised skills over generic degrees," why is the verb "prefer" used and not "prefers"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2 (Because "industries" is a plural subject)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Because "candidates" is a plural noun***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The verb form depends on the subject, not the object. “Candidates” is the object of the verb “prefer.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Because "industries" is a plural subject***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The subject of the sentence is “industries,” which is plural. Therefore, the verb must also be plural: “prefer.” If the subject were singular (“industry”), the verb would be “prefers.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Because "skills" is uncountable***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Skills” is plural, not uncountable, and it is part of the object phrase, not the subject.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Because "prefer" is always used with "now"***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adverb “now” does not affect verb conjugation. Verb form depends solely on the subject.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**: *Because "industries" is a plural subject.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Subject–verb agreement rule:** Singular subjects take singular verbs (with -s or -es), while plural subjects take the base verb form.
 
• Example: “The company **prefers** efficiency.” / “Companies **prefer** efficiency.”
 
• In the passage: “Industries prefer candidates…” → plural subject “industries” requires plural verb “prefer.”
